items.title: Benchmark indices fall amid rising crude oil prices and West Asia conflict
items.description: India's benchmark indices ended lower on Wednesday, as crude oil prices increased. The Nifty50 and Sensex experienced significant drops, falling below key levels. Midcap and smallcap stocks also saw declines, reflecting broad market weakness. Most sector indices ended in negative territory, except for FMCG and Auto. Brent crude oil prices rose, impacting investor sentiment across the market.

items.title: Stocks in news: Infosys, IndusInd Bank, Eternal, Adani Green, Dr Reddy's
items.description: Indian markets experienced a decline on Wednesday due to global and geopolitical concerns. IndusInd Bank reported a significant profit increase while Eternal saw substantial net profit growth. BPCL, however, posted a considerable loss in the first quarter. Adani Green announced a moderate profit rise, and Dr Reddy's profit declined. Several other companies like Infosys will announce their first quarter results today.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Domestic equities declined as broad-based selling persisted across sectors. India VIX surged, reflecting heightened market volatility and investor fear. Analysts expect sideways trading with a negative bias due to global tensions. Foreign portfolio investors were net sellers, impacting market sentiment negatively. The Indian rupee fell to a two-month low as oil prices climbed.

items.title: Pharma stocks slide as Trump's 100% generic drug tariff plan spooks investors
items.description: Indian drug shares declined Wednesday following US President Trump's tariff announcement.  These proposed tariffs will significantly impact companies with substantial US revenue exposure.  Analysts suggest investors should now focus on domestically oriented Indian pharmaceutical firms.  The Nifty Pharma index saw a notable decrease, while the benchmark Nifty 50 also fell.  Negotiations are expected given India's vital role in supplying affordable medicines to the US.

items.title: Mauritius tax protocol to give Indian taxman more powers to probe offshore entities
items.description: Mauritius cabinet ratified a tax protocol granting Indian officials more questioning powers.  This allows direct challenges to offshore entities suspected of tax evasion.  The principal purpose test will deny treaty benefits if tax avoidance is a primary aim.  This change follows the Tiger Global verdict and strengthens genuine substance requirements.  The protocol aims to ensure treaty benefits are for legitimate commercial purposes.

items.title: External sectors steady despite geopolitical uncertainties: RBI
items.description: India's external sector shows steady improvement, boosted by foreign investment inflows.  The economy remains strong despite global uncertainties and trade disruptions.  Foreign exchange reserves provide ample cover for imports and external debt.  Exports and imports saw strong growth in the first quarter of this fiscal year.  Bilateral trade agreements will further enhance India's external trade momentum.

items.title: Up to 451% return in 6 months! 11 smallcap stocks turn multibaggers as FIIs raise stakes for 2 straight quarters
items.description: 11 smallcaps have at least doubled in six months, led by Sterlite Technologies' 451% jump, as FIIs raised stakes across the March and June 2026 quarters. The parallel rise signals selective conviction, but analysts warn the sharp rerating leaves little room for earnings misses.

items.title: Dr Reddy’s shares crack 9% after weak Q1; these 3 brokerages slash their target prices
items.description: Dr Reddy’s shares plunged 9% on Thursday after the drugmaker reported a weak Q1 FY27 performance, with net profit tumbling 69% year-on-year to Rs 443 crore and revenue declining 6% to Rs 8,071 crore. Earnings were hit by a Rs 240 crore semaglutide API-related impact, including inventory provisions, while higher solvent and freight costs due to the Middle East conflict further squeezed EBITDA margins.

items.title: 12 stocks that Goldman Sachs, Axis, InCred Equities are bullish on. Here’s the full list
items.description: With the Nifty50 down 8% in 2026 amid the Iran war and elevated oil prices, these 12 large, mid and small cap stocks have emerged as picks from three leading brokerage firms. Here’s what investors should know.

items.title: Eternal shares jump 3% after Q1 results. Jefferies, CLSA and 4 other brokerages weigh in
items.description: Shares of Eternal climbed 3% after its Q1FY27 earnings, with brokerages reaffirming bullish views on the stock. JPMorgan, CLSA, Jefferies, Nomura, Motilal Oswal and Emkay retained positive ratings, citing accelerating growth in food delivery and Blinkit, improving quick commerce profitability, stronger margin guidance and management's confidence that competitive intensity has become more predictable.

items.title: IndusInd Bank shares fall 5% despite 72% YoY Q1 profit surge. Why analysts remain bullish?
items.description: IndusInd Bank shares fell despite reporting a 72% year-on-year jump in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 1,037 crore and brokerages raising target prices. Investors remained cautious as net interest income stayed largely flat at Rs 4,685 crore. The lender's profitability was supported by an improvement in net interest margin to 3.57%.

items.title: Sensex drops over 300 points, Nifty below 23,950 as market falls for 4th day on rising Iran-US tensions. What’s ahead?
items.description: Indian stock markets extended losses for a fourth session on Thursday. Sensex and Nifty declined as oil prices surged following US strikes on Iran. Broader market indices also saw a downward trend, with several sectors opening in the red. Escalating tensions pushed Brent crude futures above ninety-six dollars per barrel. This situation presents opportunities for long-term investors to accumulate quality stocks.

items.title: Sotefin Bharat shares set for BSE SME debut today. GMP signals muted listing
items.description: Sotefin Bharat is set to debut on the BSE SME platform on July 23, with grey market premium (GMP) trends indicating a largely flat listing. Despite subdued GMP, the Rs 89.76-crore IPO was subscribed 3.78 times overall, backed by healthy participation across investor categories. The company plans to use the IPO proceeds to expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen operations, and meet working capital needs.

items.title: Oracle Financial Services shares jump 5% on strong Q1 results; PAT soars 121%, revenue up 69%
items.description: Oracle Financial Services Software shares rose 5% on Thursday. The company reported a 121% year-on-year net income increase. Revenue from operations also saw a substantial 69% jump. New agreements with major global financial institutions were highlighted. Management attributed success to AI-first strategy and product modernization.

items.title: Emami among 4 stocks closed above VWAP, signalling bullish shift
items.description: On July 22, the closing prices of four stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied more than 1% above their Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP), according to StockEdge's technical scan data. A move above the VWAP suggests a potential bullish trend, as it indicates that the stock is trading above its average price for the session after accounting for trading volumes.When the closing price rises above the VWAP, it signifies that the closing price is higher than the average price at which the stock was traded throughout the day, with the average weighted by trading volume. Traders and investors often interpret this as a bullish signal, reflecting positive market sentiment and the possibility of continued upward momentum.

items.title: Data Patterns among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On July 22, four stocks from the Nifty500 segment that gained over 2% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from lower levels. “RSI trending up” indicates that Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are rising, suggesting strengthening momentum in the stock’s price action. This can indicate potential upward movement and is often used by traders to identify buying opportunities in momentum-driven markets.

items.title: Dividend alert! Last day to buy Bharti Airtel, Hero MotoCorp, among 43 stocks for dividend payout worth Rs 1,127
items.description: As per Sebi's T+1 settlement cycle, investors must buy a company's shares at least one trading day before the record date to ensure the shares are credited to their demat accounts in time, and they become eligible for the corporate action
